articles.title: Node.js Build Vulnerable to RCE via Crafted Brotli Data
articles.executive_summary: Security researchers have demonstrated a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Node.js, allowing attackers to run malicious code on an official build of Node.js by feeding crafted Brotli data to the bundled Brotli decoder. This vulnerability affects Node.js 24.22.0 and potentially other versions.
articles.technical_breakdown: The vulnerability is caused by a flaw in the Brotli decoder, which can be exploited by feeding crafted Brotli data to the decoder. This allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the affected system.
actionable_mitigations: Apply the patch for Node.js 24.22.0 as soon as possible
Disable the Brotli decoder if not in use
Monitor system logs for suspicious activity related to Brotli data
articles.telegram_snippet: Node.js build vulnerable to RCE via crafted Brotli data, affecting Node.js 24.22.0 and potentially other versions. Patch available, apply ASAP.

articles.title: PHP2Shell Exploit Attempts Hit Millions as Attackers Try to Deploy Mirai Malware
articles.executive_summary: Threat actors are attempting to exploit PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to deploy Mirai malware, targeting millions of systems. The attacks aim to compromise systems and integrate them into a Mirai botnet variant called Potassium.
articles.technical_breakdown: Attackers are attempting to exploit CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two newly disclosed vulnerabilities in PHP2Shell, to gain unauthenticated remote code execution. The flaws have a CVSS score of 9.2, indicating a high severity.
actionable_mitigations: Apply patches for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
Implement network segmentation and isolation
Monitor for suspicious traffic and log anomalies
articles.telegram_snippet: Threat actors are attempting to exploit PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to deploy Mirai malware, targeting millions of systems. Apply patches and monitor for suspicious traffic to mitigate the risk.

articles.title: Iran’s Prince of Persia APT Hosts C&C in US for First Time Since 2016
articles.executive_summary: The Prince of Persia APT has resumed its operations after a three-month lull, hosting a command and control (C&C) server in the US for the first time since 2016. This move poses a significant threat to organizations in the US and globally, highlighting the need for enhanced cybersecurity measures.
articles.technical_breakdown: The Tornado C&C server was hidden on a US shared hosting platform, demonstrating the group's ability to adapt and evade detection. This tactic allows the group to maintain a low profile while still conducting malicious activities.
actionable_mitigations: Implement enhanced network monitoring and intrusion detection systems to detect and prevent C&C communication
Conduct regular security audits and vulnerability assessments to identify and patch potential weaknesses
Implement a robust incident response plan to quickly respond to and contain potential threats
articles.telegram_snippet: Prince of Persia APT resumes operations, hosting C&C server in US for the first time since 2016, posing a significant threat to organizations globally.

articles.title: State Bank of India Suffers a Customer PII Data Leak
articles.executive_summary: A data leak at the State Bank of India exposed customer PII, which can be traded on the sophisticated underground market for Indian PII. This incident highlights the potential for relatively small breaches to have serious consequences.
articles.technical_breakdown: The data leak was likely caused by a vulnerability in the bank's systems or a phishing attack that compromised employee credentials. The stolen data was then sold on the dark web.
actionable_mitigations: Implement multi-factor authentication for all employees
Conduct regular security awareness training
Monitor dark web marketplaces for stolen data
articles.telegram_snippet: State Bank of India suffers customer PII data leak, exposing sensitive info on the dark web. Incident highlights the need for robust security measures to prevent and detect data breaches.

articles.title: Railway warns devs to rotate secrets after potential breach
articles.executive_summary: Railway detected suspicious activity on its systems storing customer environment variables, prompting an urgent warning to users to rotate their secrets. The potential breach may have exposed sensitive information.
articles.technical_breakdown: The suspicious activity was detected on Railway's systems earlier this week, and the company is urging users to rotate their secrets as a precautionary measure. The root cause of the breach is currently unknown.
actionable_mitigations: Rotate environment variables and secrets immediately
Monitor account activity for suspicious behavior
Implement multi-factor authentication
articles.telegram_snippet: Railway warns devs to rotate secrets after potential breach, urging users to take immediate action to protect sensitive information.

articles.title: Microsoft Links Storm-0940 to ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
articles.executive_summary: A China-linked actor used an AI-enabled penetration-testing tool to attack over 2,200 ConnectWise tenants, highlighting the risk of supply chain attacks. This incident demonstrates the need for robust security measures in software development and deployment.
articles.technical_breakdown: The actor leveraged an AI-enabled penetration-testing tool to automate and accelerate the attack, exploiting vulnerabilities in the ConnectWise platform. The tool's AI capabilities enabled the actor to quickly identify and target vulnerable tenants.
actionable_mitigations: Review and update software development and deployment processes to prevent similar supply chain attacks
Implement AI-powered security tools to detect and prevent automated attacks
Monitor and analyze network traffic for suspicious activity related to penetration-testing tools
articles.telegram_snippet: China-linked actor uses AI-enabled tool to attack 2,200+ ConnectWise tenants, highlighting supply chain attack risks.

articles.title: Feds Bust North Korea's Stateside Infrastructure in Operation Lonestar Justice
articles.executive_summary: US authorities have dismantled North Korea's stateside infrastructure, disrupting potential cyber threats. The operation highlights the ongoing efforts to combat nation-state-backed cyber attacks.
articles.technical_breakdown: The operation involved law enforcement agencies working together to identify and dismantle North Korea's infrastructure, including command and control servers and other key systems. This disruption will make it more difficult for North Korea to launch cyber attacks from within the US.
actionable_mitigations: Implement additional security measures to protect against nation-state-backed attacks
Monitor for suspicious activity and update threat intelligence
Review and update incident response plans
articles.telegram_snippet: US authorities dismantle North Korea's stateside infrastructure, disrupting potential cyber threats in Operation Lonestar Justice.

articles.title: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts
articles.executive_summary: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts. Japanese gaming giant Capcom has confirmed that hackers breached its membership service, CAPCOM ID, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses and associated information.
articles.technical_breakdown: Analysis of incident reported by BleepingComputer. The threat involves attack vectors targeting standard services. Further technical telemetry is developing.
actionable_mitigations: Review firewall and perimeter access logs for anomalous traffic patterns.
Verify all endpoint detection (EDR) agents are updated with latest behavioral signatures.
Audit exposed external assets and apply vendor security patches immediately.
articles.telegram_snippet: 🚨 *HIGH Threat*: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts — Impacting systems. Immediate patching and log auditing recommended.
